item.description:
ALC section (/alc/) ¶

This directory implements the Apache Local Community (ALC) section of the ComDev website: a landing page with an interactive map of chapters, a single chapters page that lists every chapter inline, a “start a chapter” guide, and an organizer guide. Each chapter is one Markdown data file, but by default no standalone page is generated for it (see “Chapter page model” below).

What each file is ¶

source/alc/
├── _index.md             Landing page. Intro, embedded map + chapter
│                         list (via shortcodes), how to get involved,
│                         contact. URL: /alc/
├── start-a-chapter.md     How to establish a chapter + the program rules
│                         (one-per-city, metro exceptions, CoC, quarterly
│                         reports, 3-month inactivity dissolution, no
│                         press releases). Includes the front-matter
│                         template for adding a chapter.
├── organizers.md          Practical guide for chapter organizers (running
│                         events, finding speakers, reporting, resources).
└── chapters/
    ├── _index.md          Chapter list page. URL: /alc/chapters/
    └── <city>.md          One file per chapter (the data model). Front
                           matter drives the map + list; body is the blurb
                           shown inline on the chapters page. Headless by
                           default — no standalone page (see below).

item.title: ALC Organizer Guide
item.description:
Running an ALC chapter is mostly about showing up, consistently, for your local open source community. This page collects practical help for chapter organizers.

  • Running events
  • Finding speakers
  • Topic ideas
  • Reporting
  • Resources

Running events ¶

The heart of a chapter is its events. These don’t need to be large or elaborate — a regular, reliable, welcoming meetup does far more for a community than an occasional big conference.

  • Start small and regular. A predictable monthly or quarterly cadence builds an audience.
  • Mix formats: talks, workshops, hack sessions, and informal socials all have their place.
  • Welcome newcomers explicitly. Many attendees will be students or people entirely new to open source.

Finding speakers ¶

You don’t have to find every speaker yourself.

item.title: Start an ALC Chapter
item.description:
So there’s no ALC chapter in your town or city yet, and you’d like to start one. Wonderful! Here’s what’s involved.

  • Before you apply
  • How to apply
  • Adding your chapter to this site

Before you apply ¶

  • Check the map first. There is a single ALC chapter per town or city. Look at the list of chapters to make sure one doesn’t already exist in your location.
  • For large metropolitan areas (for example the San Francisco Bay Area, or Los Angeles), more than one chapter can make sense. The ComDev PMC reviews these requests and decides on a case-by-case basis.
